messages.bing:
I am a US beginner starting with no coffee equipment. I want two milk-based espresso drinks each morning from whole beans; making them sequentially is fine. My hard limit is $800 total for all required equipment, before tax and shipping. A complete setup must grind suitably for espresso, brew espresso, and steam milk, with US household electrical compatibility. Integrated machines or separate machine-and-grinder bundles are welcome; manual steaming or automatic milk preparation is fine. Include needed basic accessories such as portafilter, baskets, tamping mechanism and milk vessel, or built-in equivalents. Optional scales, knock boxes and upgrades need not be added; ingredients and drinking cups are excluded.

Please return a strong complete setup within the limit and useful lower-cost alternatives where your catalog supports them. Include worthwhile standalone machines or espresso-capable grinders that could form a compatible bundle, even if you cannot supply every component. Explain meaningful improvements in drink consistency, beginner workflow, cleaning, dependability and seller confidence. I will pay more for justified improvements, but spending the limit is not a goal; equivalent satisfaction favors the cheaper option. Preserve cheaper credible alternatives rather than showing only the most expensive qualifying setup. Distinguish actual sellers from marketplace platforms and flag material uncertainty about variants, condition, included equipment or recourse without treating ordinary abbreviated descriptions as disqualifying. Use your existing records; do not invent missing prices or terms.
messages.google:
I am a US beginner with no coffee equipment, seeking a setup for two milk-based espresso drinks each morning from whole beans. Sequential preparation is fine. It must grind suitably for espresso, brew espresso and steam milk, and work on US household electricity. Integrated machines and separate machine-and-grinder setups are both welcome; manual steaming and automatic milk systems are acceptable. Account for basic required accessories, including a portafilter, baskets, tamping mechanism and milk vessel where applicable; built-in equivalents count. Optional scales, knock boxes and upgrades are not automatically needed. Ingredients and drinking cups are outside equipment costs.

Please emphasize good-value complete setups around $450–$650 total before tax and shipping, or lower where credible. This is a nonbinding exploration range, not my maximum budget or a required minimum spend. Include a higher-priced alternative if its likely improvement merits comparison, and useful standalone espresso grinders or machines for compatible component purchases. I value enjoyable, consistent drinks, approachable preparation of two drinks, manageable cleaning, dependability and confidence in the actual seller and recourse. The cheapest qualifying setup is not necessarily best, and higher price alone is not evidence of better results. Explain practical tradeoffs and preserve worthwhile cheaper alternatives. Identify material seller, variant, condition or package uncertainty, while allowing reasonable standard-package assumptions for credible household offers. Do not invent prices, included items or seller terms.

selected_plan.disclosure_and_withholding: Both receive functional requirements and the main satisfaction criteria. Bing receives the exact complete-equipment ceiling. Google receives a clearly nonbinding shopping range and no exact ceiling. Neither receives invented brand, condition, space or timing restrictions.
selected_plan.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Bing can target feasible complete setups but may favor offers close to $800. Google may emphasize competitively priced setups or components to improve its chance of a sale, although it may also offer costly upgrades or omit cheaper alternatives. Requests for alternatives do not override either provider's revenue incentive.
selected_plan.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Balances a budget-informed route to completeness with a second route emphasizing value and component choice. It preserves opportunities for worthwhile upgrades and mixed bundles. The asymmetric approach risks placing the budget disclosure with the less useful catalog, and Google's exploration range could steer attention away from its strongest setup.

selection_reason: The balanced split offers the best qualitative compromise: one provider can target complete setups within the actual ceiling, while the other receives a value-oriented request without the exact spending limit. Both retain the information needed to assess function, workflow and seller confidence. Assigning these roles to Bing and Google is arbitrary; no catalog evidence supports a provider-specific advantage.
